subject.title: [Feature]: Allow external runtimes to own approval presentation

question: Should OpenClaw expose a generic, opt-in channel/plugin approval-presentation ownership capability for authenticated external runtimes, with native approval prompts suppressed only for that explicit state?
rationale: This decides a semi-public Plugin SDK/channel contract and the product boundary between OpenClaw’s native approval UX and an integration’s authoritative UI; source-level mechanics cannot choose the permanent API or trust semantics safely.

options.title: Sponsor a typed ownership capability
options.body: Add a narrowly defined opt-in state that preserves authorization and structured pending events while suppressing only the duplicate native presentation.

options.title: Keep native presentation authoritative
options.body: Retain the current channel-owned approval UI and ask integrations to consume the existing approval result without suppressing OpenClaw prompts.

options.title: Route through an external plugin proposal
options.body: Keep core unchanged unless maintainers first identify a missing generic SDK seam that an external plugin cannot supply.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a typed ownership capability
recommendation.body: Add a narrowly defined opt-in state that preserves authorization and structured pending events while suppressing only the duplicate native presentation.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue explicitly requests this person’s confirmation for the contract direction.
